tour.overview:
Cusco, at 3,400 metres in the Andes, was the capital of Tawantinsuyu, the Inca Empire, which in the early 16th century stretched from Ecuador to Chile. The Incas laid out their city in the shape of a puma, with the fortress-temple of Sacsayhuamán as its head, and covered the walls of the Temple of the Sun in gold. After the Spanish conquest in 1533, churches and mansions were built on top of the Inca walls, which have survived earthquakes that toppled the colonial buildings above them. The City of Cusco has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.

This private day explains the Inca and colonial city with a licensed guide and a car. You visit the cathedral and Qorikancha, walk past the finest Inca walls to San Blas, taste your way through the San Pedro market, and drive up to Sacsayhuamán and the shrines above the city.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 7 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Cusco
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; at 3,400 to 3,700 metres altitude

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Plaza de Armas and the cathedral.
• Qorikancha and the Santo Domingo convent.
• Hatun Rumiyoc and the twelve-angled stone.
• San Blas.
• The San Pedro market.
• Sacsayhuamán, Qenqo and Cristo Blanco.

WHY THIS WORKS
We walk the compact centre and drive up the steep hill to the sites above the city, sparing your breath at altitude.

WHO IT SUITS
Everyone arriving in Cusco; ideally on your second day, after a first day of rest.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer the countryside, choose our Sacred Valley tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Cusco's altitude can cause headaches and breathlessness: rest on arrival, drink water and coca tea, and avoid heavy meals and alcohol on the first day. Photography is not allowed inside the cathedral.

days.name: The Plaza de Armas and cathedral, Qorikancha, the twelve-angled stone, San Blas, San Pedro market and Sacsayhuamán
days.description:
What to expect: the Inca and colonial heart of Cusco, with a licensed guide, private car, tickets and lunch.

Your guide meets you at your hotel at about 9:00 and walks you to the Plaza de Armas, the Inca ceremonial square of Huacaypata, now framed by colonial arcades, the Jesuit church of La Compañía and the cathedral. Built from 1560 with stones taken from Sacsayhuamán, the cathedral holds some 400 paintings of the Cusco School, in which Andean artists blended Catholic subjects with local life; in Marcos Zapata's Last Supper, Christ and the apostles share a roasted guinea pig.

You walk along Hatun Rumiyoc, a street of Inca walls that belonged to the palace of the emperor Inca Roca, to see the famous twelve-angled stone, fitted so perfectly that a blade cannot pass between the joints. You climb to San Blas, the artisans' quarter of whitewashed houses, blue balconies and workshops. Then you visit Qorikancha, the Temple of the Sun, once covered in sheets of gold and filled with life-size golden plants and animals, which the Spaniards melted down; the Dominicans built their convent on top, and its Inca chambers, curved wall and precise stonework are exposed inside the cloister.

After lunch, you stop at the San Pedro market, among stalls of exotic fruit, giant corn, potatoes of every colour and fresh juices. Your driver then takes you up to Sacsayhuamán, overlooking the city. Its three tiers of zigzag walls are made of limestone blocks of up to 120 tonnes, fitted without mortar; here Manco Inca's rebellion against the Spanish fought its decisive battle in 1536, and every 24 June the festival of Inti Raymi is re-enacted on its esplanade. You also see Qenqo, a limestone outcrop carved with channels, steps and an underground altar used for rituals, and the view over Cusco from the Cristo Blanco statue. You are back at your hotel at about 16:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
09:00 – Meeting at your hotel.
09:15 – Plaza de Armas and the cathedral.
10:45 – Hatun Rumiyoc and San Blas.
11:45 – Qorikancha.
13:00 – Lunch.
14:15 – San Pedro market.
15:00 – Sacsayhuamán, Qenqo and Cristo Blanco.
16:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A sunset visit to Sacsayhuamán is lovely; the order can be reversed.
• The Museo de Arte Precolombino or the Inka Museum can be added.
• Pickpockets operate in crowded markets; keep valuables close.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, entrance tickets, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: market tastings, drinks with lunch, tips.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: When should we do this tour?
faq.answer: Ideally on your second day in Cusco, after resting on the first to adjust to the altitude.

faq.question: Are the tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes: the cathedral, Qorikancha and the tourist ticket covering Sacsayhuamán and Qenqo.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, at a local restaurant. Vegetarian and other diets are easy to arrange.

faq.question: Is the altitude a problem?
faq.answer: Cusco is at 3,400 metres. Walk slowly, drink water and coca tea, and tell your guide if you feel unwell; the car is always nearby.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the giant stones of Sacsayhuamán and the market. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The centre has steep cobbled streets; the car can drop you at each site.

faq.question: Can we take photos in the cathedral?
faq.answer: No, photography is not allowed in the cathedral. It is allowed at Qorikancha and the Inca sites.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Peru but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Layers, as it is cold in the shade and hot in the sun, a hat, sun cream and comfortable shoes.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: April to October is dry and sunny. June is festival month, with Inti Raymi on 24 June.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
